items.detail: The **Nasdaq** rose 0.64% to 27,366.17 Friday and the S&P 500 gained 0.59% to 7,811.54. That ended a two-day slide and gave both indices a weekly gain.
items.why: OpenAI told investors it expects $70 billion in annual revenue by year-end, easing fears and lifting chip stocks.

items.detail: Brent fell about 1.3% to near **$103** Friday, giving back part of Thursday's jump, though it still finished the week higher.
items.why: Trump called the Iran talks productive and said the US would not strike Iran before the November 3 midterms.

items.detail: Earnings season starts next week with the biggest banks, while the **10-year Treasury yield** held near 5.24% Friday.
Hong Kong's **Hang Seng** jumped 1.79% to 24,211.35 Friday, led by a 3.1% rise in the tech index. Korea and Taiwan were shut for holidays.
items.why: Bargain hunters bought beaten-down Tencent, Xiaomi and other platform stocks as global chip shares bounced back.

items.detail: The **Nifty** rebounded about 1.3% to 22,520.45 Friday, pulling away from its 52-week low, and the Sensex added 879 points.
items.why: Oil prices easing on Trump's Iran comments set off broad buying, with IT stocks leading.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** rose **0.46%** to 2,806.98 Friday but trailed the bigger indices, and it is still about 9% below its August high.
items.why: Yields barely moved from about 5.2% after the Fed's September hike, which kept pressure on rate-sensitive small firms.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** held near **$82,600** early Saturday after a fourth straight losing day briefly took it below $81,000.
items.why: Spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $729 million over two sessions before Friday's early data showed a small inflow.

items.detail: **Ether** stayed around **$2,500** Friday, up from a midweek low near $2,406, but it has not yet mounted a clear recovery.
items.why: US spot ether ETFs posted an eighth straight day of outflows, and heavy long liquidations hurt sentiment.

items.detail: **Solana** slid about 4.7% to around **$110** Friday, even though its network switched to faster 200-millisecond blocks the same day.
items.why: Standard Chartered cut its 2026 target to $250 from $310, and Solana ETFs kept losing money.

items.detail: **Gold** rose about 1.3% to near **$4,194** Friday, briefly going above $4,200 as it extended its recovery from a two-month low.
items.why: A weaker dollar, lower Treasury yields and easing fears of a US-Iran clash made gold more attractive.

crossCuttingTheme: Trump's pledge not to strike Iran before the midterms pulled Brent back toward $103, easing inflation fears and lifting US tech, Hong Kong, India and gold. Crypto stayed weak because ETF outflows outweighed the relief.
